chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Ayub ibn Nuh from Safwan ibn Yahya from Khuzaymah ibn Yaqtin from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj from Bukayr from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The mother's share is never reduced from one-third, except in the presence of children and siblings, when the father is alive."
ai.seo_question: When does the mother's inheritance share remain one-third instead of being reduced to one-sixth?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies a specific scenario in Shia inheritance jurisprudence where the mother retains her full one-third share rather than being reduced to one-sixth, provided the deceased is survived by the father, children, and siblings. It highlights the distinct role of the father as a primary heir who does not trigger the reduction clause for the mother, a nuance emphasized by scholars like Al-Tusi in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*. This ruling underscores the stability of the mother's portion in complex family structures where multiple direct descendants and the father coexist.
